1|# Design: task 8 scene by scene reader
2|
3|Goal: replace continuous scroll with one scene view at a time, so the next plot turn never sits on screen and music changes only on scene entry. Branch `scene-reader`. This step writes only this doc.
4|
5|## Owner decision
6|
7|Continuous scroll is rejected. It shows the next scene before its turn and moves the music by scroll position.
8|
9|## Route and file layout
10|
11|```text
12|app/page.tsx                redirect to /leer/<first scene id>
13|app/leer/layout.tsx         server shell, slim meta, mounts music container
14|app/leer/[sceneId]/page.tsx server view, one scene only, generateStaticParams
15|app/leer/scene-page.tsx     client pager, keys, buttons, progress, focus
16|app/reader.tsx              music container, driven by route scene id
17|app/player.tsx              unchanged audio engine
18|app/player-controls.tsx     unchanged buttons from task 6
19|core/reader.ts              pagination, scene view, nav reducer, entry check
20|scripts/check-isolation.mjs post build scene isolation scan
21|```
22|
23|`/` redirects server side to the first scene id. Choice: one address per scene keeps jumps and the demo selector trivial.
24|
25|## Pure core pieces
26|
27|All pure logic lives in `core/reader.ts`. Choice: it already owns scene shapes, so no new module is needed.
28|
29|```ts
30|export interface SubPage { paragraphs: ReaderParagraph[]; startN: number; endN: number; words: number; }
31|export function paginateScene(paragraphs: ReaderParagraph[], budgetWords: number): SubPage[];
32|
33|export interface SceneView {
34|  sceneId: string; ch: number; chapterTitle: string; title: string;
35|  emotion: SceneSignal | null; pages: SubPage[];
36|  prevSceneId: string | null; nextSceneId: string | null;
37|  k: number; n: number;
38|}
39|export function buildSceneView(model: ReaderModel, sceneId: string, budgetWords: number): SceneView;
40|
41|export interface NavState { sceneId: string; page: number; }
42|export type NavAction =
43|  | { kind: "next" } | { kind: "prev" }
44|  | { kind: "goto"; sceneId: string; atEnd?: boolean };
45|export interface NavIndex { order: string[]; pageCounts: Map<string, number>; }
46|export function navReducer(state: NavState, action: NavAction, index: NavIndex): NavState;
47|
48|export function isSceneEntry(prevSceneId: string | null, nextSceneId: string): boolean;
49|```
50|
51|`paginateScene` splits by word count at paragraph boundaries and never splits a paragraph. An oversize paragraph takes its own page. An empty scene returns one empty page. Choice: boundary only rule keeps emotion uniform inside a scene.
52|
53|`buildSceneView` throws on unknown scene id. Choice: fail loudly at build time so a bad id never ships an empty page.
54|
55|`navReducer` crosses chapters through the global scene order. Next on the last sub-page enters the next scene at page 0. Prev on the first sub-page enters the previous scene at its last page. Bounds are no-ops. Unknown goto id keeps state. Choice: a reducer keeps every move in one testable place.
56|
57|`isSceneEntry` returns true only when the scene id changed. Choice: one predicate lets the container prove that sub-page moves never touch the scheduler.
58|
59|## Page budget
60|
61|Budget is 250 words per sub-page. Oz averages 35 words per paragraph and 8.3 paragraphs per scene, so most scenes fit one or two views and the longest fits about three. 250 words fill a desktop view at the 65ch measure without scroll.
62|
63|## Where state lives
64|
65|Scene id lives in the route and is the only source of truth. Sub-page index lives in client state inside `scene-page.tsx`, keyed by scene id so it resets on entry. "Enter at last sub-page" travels as `?at=end`, set only by the Prev button through `router.push`, read once on mount. Choice: intent stays in the URL because back and forward then land on the same sub-page.
66|
67|## Layout and audio persistence
68|
69|`app/leer/layout.tsx` mounts the music container once, so its state and the audio elements survive scene navigations. The container reads the current scene id with `useParams` inside `app/reader.tsx`. The scene page passes only the current signal down as a prop. Choice: params in the client container avoid threading ids through server props on every move.
70|
71|Navigation uses `router.push` and `router.replace` only, never prefetched links. Choice: no prefetch keeps other scenes out of the client cache.
72|
73|## What data reaches the client
74|
75|The layout receives slim meta for all scenes: `{ id, ch, emotion }` plus the chapter table `[{ ch, title }]`. The scene page receives current scene text and title only. No other scene text, titles, or summaries ship. Choice: titles can spoil, but the scheduler needs every emotion vector and the jump needs chapter titles.
76|
77|## Keyboard and focus
78|
79|ArrowRight moves next, ArrowLeft moves prev. Keys are ignored with modifier keys and while focus sits in an input, select, textarea, or contenteditable element. Buttons read "Anterior" and "Siguiente" and disable at book start and end. On scene change focus moves to the text heading and the view scrolls to top. No announcement. Choice: silent focus keeps keyboard users oriented without noise.
80|

82|

1|# Contracts
2|
3|Music generation must never block the reader. Each module below owns one
4|job and can be swapped without touching the others. Import direction is
5|`core <- server` and `core <- app`. Server and client components never
6|import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client
7|files never do.
8|
9|## Book data
10|
11|`data/books/oz/book.json` holds the frozen text: id, title, author,
12|`textVersion` hash, chapters with `start_n` and `end_n`, and paragraphs
13|with `id`, `ch`, `n`, and `text`. `analysis.json` is the scene source
14|the reader consumes: the same scenes plus Jev vectors, the Muse
15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.
19|`core/reader.ts` defines `buildReaderModel`, which joins paragraphs to
20|scenes by ordinal range and throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs
21|covered zero or two times.
22|
23|## Scene reader
24|
25|One static route per scene (`app/leer/[sceneId]`, `dynamicParams`
26|false); `/` redirects to the first scene. The layout mounts the music
27|container once and passes slim metadata for all scenes: id, chapter,
28|and emotion triple only. Each scene page builds its view with
29|`buildSceneView` and ships only that scene's text, its chapter title,
30|and neighbor ids. Sub-pages come from `paginateScene` (250 words, split
31|at paragraph boundaries). The pager moves sub-pages in client state and
32|pushes routes with `router.push`, never `<Link>`; going back lands on
33|the previous scene's last sub-page via `?at=end`. The client never
34|receives other scenes' text, titles, or summaries.
35|
36|## Music library
37|
38|The library is a static `public/music/manifest.json`, version 3, fetched
39|by the client from `/music/manifest.json`. A static file needs no route,
40|ships from the CDN, and swaps by replacing files only. Tracks may be
41|several minutes long and are not loops unless marked so. A version 2
42|manifest migrates inline to one implicit `default` soundtrack of style
43|`orchestral`.
44|
45|`MusicManifest = { version, styles, soundtracks, tracks, playlists }`.
46|`StyleInfo = { id, name }` where `id` is a lowercase slug and `name` is
47|the Spanish display name. `Soundtrack = { id, name, style }` plus
48|optional `credit`. `Track = { id, src, title, emotion, vector,
49|intensity, tempo, durationSec, soundtrack, style }` plus optional
50|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
51|loop), `loop` (default true), `source` (`generated`, `jamendo`, or
52|`recording`), `artist`, `composer`, `license`, `attribution`, and
53|`sourceUrl` (https only). `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
54|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
55|entries in 0..1. Every track names a soundtrack id, every track style
56|matches its soundtrack style, and every style is a listed style id.
57|`core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects unknown versions,
58|duplicate ids, unknown soundtrack or style ids, style mismatches,
59|missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range numbers,
60|`startSec` outside its range, unknown `source` values, a non-boolean
61|`playlistOnly`, and any `src`
62|that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. A soundtrack with no
63|tracks parses. The reader calls it on every fetch, so a bad drop-in
64|fails loudly in dev. Remote URLs need a `media-src` addition in
65|`next.config.ts`.
66|
67|`Track.playlistOnly` defaults to false. A true value marks a playlist
68|only track: it still names a soundtrack and style, but no emotion pick
69|ever returns it. `MusicManifest.playlists` holds
70|`Playlist = { id, label, trackIds }` entries, most notably
71|`just-play-chopin`. A missing key parses as an empty list, and a v2
72|migration gives an empty list. Parse rejects duplicate playlist ids,
73|empty labels, non-array `trackIds`, and any `trackIds` entry that names
74|no track, with the playlist and the id in the message.
75|
76|## Soundtracks and selection
77|
78|One soundtrack plays at a time. `MusicSelection = { mode, soundtrackId,
79|style }` is the session: `style` scopes every pick, `soundtrackId` is
80|the home in `soundtrack` mode, `mode` picks the ranking rule. The style
81|is the user's choice, changed with the style selector. The initial
82|soundtrack is the one covering the most hand-labeled emotions, ties by
83|lower id; a valid persisted id wins. The session persists `{ mode,
84|soundtrackId, style }` in localStorage under `lectoria.music.v1`. On
85|load a stored style with no tracks and a stored soundtrack outside the
86|stored style fall back to the defaults. Storage exceptions never break
87|playback.
88|
89|In `soundtrack` mode each scene scores only the session soundtrack. When
90|the soundtrack has no track with the scene emotion, the scheduler borrows
91|the best same-style track for that scene only and reports `fallback`, so
92|the bar can say `de otra banda sonora`. In `random` mode each scheduled
93|select draws among same-style tracks with the scene emotion (or the best
94|same-style tracks when the emotion is missing) within `randomTolerance`
95|(0.05) of the best score, keeps the current track when it is eligible,
96|and avoids an immediate repeat otherwise. Dwell and min-track rules hold
97|in both modes. The core never calls `Math.random`; the reader injects it
98|and tests pass a seeded stub.
99|
100|## Change track, mix toggle, style change
101|
102|`nextTrack` cycles same-emotion tracks in score order, wrapping and
103|skipping the current. In `soundtrack` mode it stays inside the current
104|soundtrack first, then tries the same emotion in other same-style
105|soundtracks, then the best same-style track overall. In `random` mode it
106|ranges over all same-style soundtracks at once. A null scene cycles the
107|style set in id order.
108|
109|The `Mezclar bandas` toggle flips `mode`. Turning it off keeps the
110|soundtrack of the playing track. `requestStyleChange` moves the session
111|to the best-coverage soundtrack of the new style and picks the best
112|match for the scene inside that soundtrack, or the best same-style track
113|by score when the picked soundtrack lacks the scene emotion. It never
114|crosses styles. The scheduler applies it at once with the normal
115|crossfade and holds the choice like a Next. There is no
116|soundtrack-change button.
117|
118|## Playlist mode
119|
120|`SchedulerState.playlist` holds `{ id, index }` while a fixed playlist
121|plays. `enterPlaylist` switches at once to the first `trackIds` entry
122|with `crossfadeSec`, no dwell and no min-track rule. While it is on,
123|scene changes update the active scene but never switch, `requestNext`
124|and `noteTrackEnded` advance to the next entry in order and wrap from
125|the last to the first, and playlist tracks run to their end because the
126|player forces looping off. `exitPlaylist` clears the playlist state and
127|switches at once to the best match for the current scene under the
128|restored selection. The mode is never persisted, so a reload returns to
129|emotion mode. The mix toggle and the style selector stay disabled while
130|it is on, and the style list hides styles with only playlist tracks.
131|
132|## Similarity and config
133|
134|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
135|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
136|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
137|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
138|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
139|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
140|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
141|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
142|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
143|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
144|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
145|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
146|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id. Route entries use
147|`sceneEntryDwellSec` (5) as the dwell override; scoring, hysteresis,
148|and overrides are unchanged.
149|
150|## Selection scheduler
151|
152|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
153|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
154|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
155|timers. The reader cues music on scene entry only: one `observeScene`
156|call per route id, gated by an id comparison, so sub-page moves never
157|reach the scheduler. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
158|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
159|with the scene it belongs to.
160|
161|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
162|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
163|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
164|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
165|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
166|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
167|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
168|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a
169|skip override stands: ticks return no change while it is set, and only
170|a new scene promotion clears it. A switch
171|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
172|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
173|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
174|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
175|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
176|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
177|skip override.
178|
179|## Player
180|
181|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
182|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
183|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
184|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
185|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
186|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
187|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
188|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
189|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
190|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
191|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
192|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
193|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
194|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
195|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
196|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
197|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
198|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
199|
200|The bar shows Play/Pause, Volume, a Cambiar track button (disabled when
201|Next has nothing to offer), a Mezclar bandas toggle with `aria-pressed`,
202|and a style selector listing only styles that have tracks (hidden while
203|fewer than two qualify). A `Just play Chopin` toggle appears only when
204|the manifest defines that playlist with tracks; its text comes from the
205|playlist label, it carries `aria-pressed`, and it shows the Meta blue
206|accent while pressed. It shows the track title with its emotion
207|label, the soundtrack name, and attribution when present: composer or
208|artist, license, and a source link. While the playlist plays, the bar
209|hides the emotion label and the fallback note. A fallback pick adds the
210|quiet note
211|`de otra banda sonora`. On manifest failure the reader still renders and
212|the bar shows a short neutral note. UI motion stays under 200 ms.
213|Controls are real buttons and inputs with labels, visible focus, and
214|keyboard use. `app/player.tsx` keeps the audio engine and bar layout;
215|`app/player-controls.tsx` holds the buttons and the style selector;
216|`app/music-prefs.ts` owns the storage helper.
217|
218|## Image api
219|
220|`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
221|discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
222|the paragraph where the selection starts, `{ kind: "scene", bookId,
223|textVersion, sceneId }` names the scene. Validation is strict: known
224|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, known
225|`sceneId`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic Spanish message.
226|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text. "Ilustrar
227|escena" uses the scene id from the route.
228|
229|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
230|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
231|when another request holds the lock, in which case the client reposts
232|every 3 s up to about 2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
233|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `unavailable`, or `bad_request` with a
234|friendly Spanish message. Caption is the scene title for scenes and the
235|first words of the paragraph for passages, built server-side.
236|
237|The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
238|plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key is book plus scene id plus
239|the same versions. Both map to a deterministic Blob path
240|(`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis
241|index maps key to Blob URL, so hits are one GET; on an index miss the
242|server lists by exact path prefix (head equivalent) before generating
243|and backfills the index.
244|A Redis lock per key returns `pending` to concurrent requests. Quota is
245|5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed cookie,
246|whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
247|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10). Failures refund
248|quota and budget and release the lock.
249|
250|## Chat api
251|
252|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
253|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
254|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
255|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
256|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
257|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
258|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
259|
260|## Quotas and budget
261|
262|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
263|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
264|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
265|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
266|the client, details stay in server logs.

15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.
19|`core/reader.ts` defines `buildReaderModel`, which joins paragraphs to
20|scenes by ordinal range and throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs
21|covered zero or two times.
22|
23|## Scene reader
24|
25|One static route per scene (`app/leer/[sceneId]`, `dynamicParams`
26|false); `/` redirects to the first scene. The layout mounts the music
27|container once and passes slim metadata for all scenes: id, chapter,
28|and emotion triple only. Each scene page builds its view with
29|`buildSceneView` and ships only that scene's text, its chapter title,
30|and neighbor ids. Sub-pages come from `paginateScene` (250 words, split
31|at paragraph boundaries). The pager moves sub-pages in client state and
32|pushes routes with `router.push`, never `<Link>`; going back lands on
33|the previous scene's last sub-page via `?at=end`. The client never
34|receives other scenes' text, titles, or summaries.
35|
36|## Music library
37|
38|The library is a static `public/music/manifest.json`, version 3, fetched
39|by the client from `/music/manifest.json`. A static file needs no route,
40|ships from the CDN, and swaps by replacing files only. Tracks may be
41|several minutes long and are not loops unless marked so. A version 2
42|manifest migrates inline to one implicit `default` soundtrack of style
43|`orchestral`.
44|
45|`MusicManifest = { version, styles, soundtracks, tracks, playlists }`.
46|`StyleInfo = { id, name }` where `id` is a lowercase slug and `name` is
47|the Spanish display name. `Soundtrack = { id, name, style }` plus
48|optional `credit`. `Track = { id, src, title, emotion, vector,
49|intensity, tempo, durationSec, soundtrack, style }` plus optional
50|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
51|loop), `loop` (default true), `source` (`generated`, `jamendo`, or
52|`recording`), `artist`, `composer`, `license`, `attribution`, and
53|`sourceUrl` (https only). `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
54|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
55|entries in 0..1. Every track names a soundtrack id, every track style
56|matches its soundtrack style, and every style is a listed style id.
57|`core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects unknown versions,
58|duplicate ids, unknown soundtrack or style ids, style mismatches,
59|missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range numbers,
60|`startSec` outside its range, unknown `source` values, a non-boolean
61|`playlistOnly`, and any `src`
62|that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. A soundtrack with no
63|tracks parses. The reader calls it on every fetch, so a bad drop-in
64|fails loudly in dev. Remote URLs need a `media-src` addition in
65|`next.config.ts`.
66|
67|`Track.playlistOnly` defaults to false. A true value marks a playlist
68|only track: it still names a soundtrack and style, but no emotion pick
69|ever returns it. `MusicManifest.playlists` holds
70|`Playlist = { id, label, trackIds }` entries, most notably
71|`just-play-chopin`. A missing key parses as an empty list, and a v2
72|migration gives an empty list. Parse rejects duplicate playlist ids,
73|empty labels, non-array `trackIds`, and any `trackIds` entry that names
74|no track, with the playlist and the id in the message.
75|
76|## Soundtracks and selection
77|
78|One soundtrack plays at a time. `MusicSelection = { mode, soundtrackId,
79|style }` is the session: `style` scopes every pick, `soundtrackId` is
80|the home in `soundtrack` mode, `mode` picks the ranking rule. The style
81|is the user's choice, changed with the style selector. The initial
82|soundtrack is the one covering the most hand-labeled emotions, ties by
83|lower id; a valid persisted id wins. The session persists `{ mode,
84|soundtrackId, style }` in localStorage under `lectoria.music.v1`. On
85|load a stored style with no tracks and a stored soundtrack outside the
86|stored style fall back to the defaults. Storage exceptions never break
87|playback.
88|
89|In `soundtrack` mode each scene scores only the session soundtrack. When
90|the soundtrack has no track with the scene emotion, the scheduler borrows
91|the best same-style track for that scene only and reports `fallback`, so
92|the bar can say `de otra banda sonora`. In `random` mode each scheduled
93|select draws among same-style tracks with the scene emotion (or the best
94|same-style tracks when the emotion is missing) within `randomTolerance`
95|(0.05) of the best score, keeps the current track when it is eligible,
96|and avoids an immediate repeat otherwise. Dwell and min-track rules hold
97|in both modes. The core never calls `Math.random`; the reader injects it
98|and tests pass a seeded stub.
99|
100|## Change track, mix toggle, style change
101|
102|`nextTrack` cycles same-emotion tracks in score order, wrapping and
103|skipping the current. In `soundtrack` mode it stays inside the current
104|soundtrack first, then tries the same emotion in other same-style
105|soundtracks, then the best same-style track overall. In `random` mode it
106|ranges over all same-style soundtracks at once. A null scene cycles the
107|style set in id order.
108|
109|The `Mezclar bandas` toggle flips `mode`. Turning it off keeps the
110|soundtrack of the playing track. `requestStyleChange` moves the session
111|to the best-coverage soundtrack of the new style and picks the best
112|match for the scene inside that soundtrack, or the best same-style track
113|by score when the picked soundtrack lacks the scene emotion. It never
114|crosses styles. The scheduler applies it at once with the normal
115|crossfade and holds the choice like a Next. There is no
116|soundtrack-change button.
117|
118|## Playlist mode
119|
120|`SchedulerState.playlist` holds `{ id, index }` while a fixed playlist
121|plays. `enterPlaylist` switches at once to the first `trackIds` entry
122|with `crossfadeSec`, no dwell and no min-track rule. While it is on,
123|scene changes update the active scene but never switch, `requestNext`
124|and `noteTrackEnded` advance to the next entry in order and wrap from
125|the last to the first, and playlist tracks run to their end because the
126|player forces looping off. `exitPlaylist` clears the playlist state and
127|switches at once to the best match for the current scene under the
128|restored selection. The mode is never persisted, so a reload returns to
129|emotion mode. The mix toggle and the style selector stay disabled while
130|it is on, and the style list hides styles with only playlist tracks.
131|
132|## Similarity and config
133|
134|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
135|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
136|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
137|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
138|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
139|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
140|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
141|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
142|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
143|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
144|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
145|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
146|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id. Route entries use
147|`sceneEntryDwellSec` (5) as the dwell override; scoring, hysteresis,
148|and overrides are unchanged.
149|
150|## Selection scheduler
151|
152|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
153|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
154|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
155|timers. The reader cues music on scene entry only: one `observeScene`
156|call per route id, gated by an id comparison, so sub-page moves never
157|reach the scheduler. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
158|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
159|with the scene it belongs to.
160|
161|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
162|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
163|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
164|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
165|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
166|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
167|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
168|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a
169|skip override stands: ticks return no change while it is set, and only
170|a new scene promotion clears it. A switch
171|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
172|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
173|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
174|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
175|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
176|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
177|skip override.
178|
179|## Player
180|
181|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
182|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
183|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
184|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
185|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
186|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
187|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
188|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
189|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
190|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
191|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
192|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
193|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
194|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
195|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
196|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
197|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
198|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
199|
200|The bar shows Play/Pause, Volume, a Cambiar track button (disabled when
201|Next has nothing to offer), a Mezclar bandas toggle with `aria-pressed`,
202|and a style selector listing only styles that have tracks (hidden while
203|fewer than two qualify). A `Just play Chopin` toggle appears only when
204|the manifest defines that playlist with tracks; its text comes from the
205|playlist label, it carries `aria-pressed`, and it shows the Meta blue
206|accent while pressed. It shows the track title with its emotion
207|label, the soundtrack name, and attribution when present: composer or
208|artist, license, and a source link. While the playlist plays, the bar
209|hides the emotion label and the fallback note. A fallback pick adds the
210|quiet note
211|`de otra banda sonora`. On manifest failure the reader still renders and
212|the bar shows a short neutral note. UI motion stays under 200 ms.
213|Controls are real buttons and inputs with labels, visible focus, and
214|keyboard use. `app/player.tsx` keeps the audio engine and bar layout;
215|`app/player-controls.tsx` holds the buttons and the style selector;
216|`app/music-prefs.ts` owns the storage helper.
217|
218|## Image api
219|
220|`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
221|discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
222|the paragraph where the selection starts, `{ kind: "scene", bookId,
223|textVersion, sceneId }` names the scene. Validation is strict: known
224|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, known
225|`sceneId`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic Spanish message.
226|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text. "Ilustrar
227|escena" uses the scene id from the route.
228|
229|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
230|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
231|when another request holds the lock, in which case the client reposts
232|every 3 s up to about 2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
233|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `unavailable`, or `bad_request` with a
234|friendly Spanish message. Caption is the scene title for scenes and the
235|first words of the paragraph for passages, built server-side.
236|
237|The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
238|plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key is book plus scene id plus
239|the same versions. Both map to a deterministic Blob path
240|(`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis
241|index maps key to Blob URL, so hits are one GET; on an index miss the
242|server lists by exact path prefix (head equivalent) before generating
243|and backfills the index.
244|A Redis lock per key returns `pending` to concurrent requests. Quota is
245|5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed cookie,
246|whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
247|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10). Failures refund
248|quota and budget and release the lock.
249|
250|## Chat api
251|
252|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
253|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
254|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
255|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
256|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
257|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
258|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
259|
260|## Quotas and budget
261|
262|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
263|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
264|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
265|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
266|the client, details stay in server logs.

<skill-body id="ponytail-review">
---
name: ponytail-review
description: >
  Quality review of a change: is the logic right, is it safe, does it hold
  under real load, is risky code tested, is it fast enough, and is every line
  needed. Reads the connected code, not only the diff. Each finding is
  explained in plain English. Use for "review this", "code review", "review
  the last commit", "review my PR", "is this over-engineered", /ponytail-review.
---

Review a change like the senior developer who will be paged when it breaks.
Order of importance: correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean.
Lean still matters: every extra line must be read, tested and fixed later.
This is a report the user asked for, so give it in full.

## 1. Understand first

- Review what the user names: uncommitted or staged changes, a branch, a PR
  link, or files. Nothing named: the uncommitted changes, or the last commit
  if there are none.
- Read the diff, then the code it touches: callers of every changed function,
  the functions it calls, the tests, the README.
- Trace the real flow: where data comes in, what is stored, what goes out.
- A change can break code it does not touch. When a signature, return value
  or behavior changes, grep every caller.
- Find the expected load in the repo (README, deploy config): one person
  running a script, or many users and processes at once. Judge scale against
  that, and say which load you assumed.

## 2. Look for

1. **Bug:** wrong result, crash, missed edge case (empty, zero, last item,
   rounding, time zones), a caller broken by the change, a fix applied in one
   caller while the shared function stays broken.
2. **Risk:** security holes (injection, weak randomness, secrets, missing
   checks on input from users), data loss (errors swallowed, writes in the
   wrong order, no transaction).
3. **Scale:** fine for one user, wrong for many: check-then-write races, the
